section_summary: This section consists chiefly of FBI reports and State Department correspondence about suspected Japanese espionage and propaganda in Argentina during the Second World War. The reports examine informants, mail drops, shipping and trading firms, newspaper subscriptions, and contacts with the former Japanese Embassy in Buenos Aires. Later correspondence requests information from Japanese archives and supplies Argentine officials with allegations about Kingo Kawai’s maritime espionage network.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Tomiya Koseki and Carlos Santa Cruz
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential memorandum on Carlos Santa Cruz’s wartime work for Japanese interests in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the enclosed Santa Cruz memorandum and notes that the American embassies in Buenos Aires and Santiago received the information.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Carlos Santa Cruz and Japanese activities in Argentina
subfiles.about: Reconstructs Carlos Santa Cruz’s connections with Japanese diplomats, Chilean nationalists, suspected couriers and espionage schemes.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum recounts Santa Cruz’s nationalist activity in Chile, his move to Buenos Aires, and his dealings with Shozo Murai and other Japanese Embassy personnel. It describes payments, propaganda publications, coded correspondence carried by Alberto Veloz, proposed maritime observation, and allegations concerning maps and mail drops. It compares Santa Cruz’s statements with Argentine police questioning and other sources, including testimony about the Goyo family and Armando Puentes. It closes with Santa Cruz’s return to Chile and Argentine action against Humberto Goyo.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Julio Guido Amuchástegui
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on Amuchástegui’s wartime activities for Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the enclosed report and says the American Embassy in Buenos Aires has the information.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Julio Guido Amuchástegui
subfiles.about: Examines Amuchástegui’s suspected receipt of foreign publications for the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Investigators found no current Japanese contact but identified a 1941 Embassy payment for American newspaper and magazine subscriptions in Amuchástegui’s name.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Henri Catherin Gravet and Elías Jofré
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on Gravet’s and Jofré’s wartime activities for the Japanese in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the enclosed memorandum to State and notes distribution to the American embassies in Buenos Aires and Santiago.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Henri Catherin Gravet and Elías Jofré
subfiles.about: Reviews Gravet’s arrival in Buenos Aires and Jofré’s alleged liaison and periodical-collection work for the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Argentine police questioning portrayed Jofré as collecting Allied publications through post-office boxes for Shozo Murai and meeting Gravet when he arrived by ship. The memorandum also recounts Jofré’s imprisonment and later inquiries into Gravet’s other Buenos Aires contacts.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Nobuo Yatoh and Magoichi Hiramatsu
subfiles.about: Forwards source information on Hiramatsu’s statements about suspected Japanese agent Nobuo Yatoh.
subfiles.summary: Links Hiramatsu to an address book found on Yatoh and forwards the enclosed investigation.

subfiles.title: Duplicate FBI transmittal concerning Nobuo Yatoh
subfiles.about: Repeats the transmittal of information about Hiramatsu’s account of Yatoh.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the preceding transmittal letter.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Nobuo Yatoh and Magoichi Hiramatsu
subfiles.about: Investigates Hiramatsu’s correspondence with Yatoh and names found in Yatoh’s notebook.
subfiles.summary: Hiramatsu denied espionage and said he forwarded Yatoh’s radio messages from Bolivia as a favor. Investigators traced his employment and business interests, Natalio Dimsitz and García y Compañía, and the Hanschke family at an address recorded in Yatoh’s notebook. A separate source identified Arturo Hanschke as a reported Nazi agent.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Osaka Shosen Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.about: Forwards an interview with the Japanese shipping firm’s accountant Enrique Saban.
subfiles.summary: Introduces Saban’s account of subscriptions to American periodicals for his Japanese employers.

subfiles.title: Interview with Osaka Shosen accountant Enrique Saban
subfiles.about: Documents periodical subscriptions and the financial state of Osaka Shosen’s Argentine branch.
subfiles.summary: Saban admitted obtaining Allied newspapers and magazines for Japanese staff, who studied shipping and aircraft information. He described subscriptions placed under employees’ names and the branch’s near-liquidation.

subfiles.title: Strategic Services Unit transmittal concerning Boris Sapiro
subfiles.about: Transmits information about Boris Sapiro to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the attached memorandum and notes that the FBI is also receiving the information.

subfiles.title: Boris Sapiro’s voyage from Shanghai toward Argentina
subfiles.about: Reports travel by an alleged former Japanese Gendarmerie agent bound for Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Reports Sapiro’s March 11 sailing from Shanghai aboard the Doctor Lykes, with a United States transit visa.

subfiles.title: State Department forwarding of Boris Sapiro report
subfiles.about: Sends the Strategic Services Unit report on Boris Sapiro to Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the April 2 report for the Embassy’s information.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Nambei Trading Company and Mitsui personnel
subfiles.about: Forwards additional findings on Isoma Kobayashi and Japanese firms’ review of Allied publications.
subfiles.summary: Highlights Kobayashi’s statement that Nambei personnel supplied information from Allied publications to the Japanese Embassy.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Mitsui and Nambei Trading Company personnel
subfiles.about: Reviews alleged intelligence collection by Japanese trading firms and their associates in Argentina and Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum records Kobayashi’s police statements and later interviews about extracting economic and other information from Allied publications for the Japanese Embassy. It follows Mitsui and Nambei personnel, suspected mail-drop addresses, post-office boxes, and related contacts in Chile and Brazil. Later inquiries concern Sukekazu Miura, Taro Sukugawa, Sidney Carlos Smith, platinum dealings, and a map marked in Uruguay.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Ofelia P. Fernández
subfiles.about: Forwards information on an Argentine government employee suspected of Japanese espionage.
subfiles.summary: Introduces the enclosed investigation of Fernández’s contacts with Japanese Embassy officials.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Ofelia P. Fernández
subfiles.about: Examines Fernández’s employment, finances, Japanese contacts and movements.
subfiles.summary: Investigators found extensive Japanese social contacts but no observed subversive activity; the report describes her government work, acquaintances, correspondence and vacations.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese archival information
subfiles.about: Asks when information from Japanese government and other archives on subversion in Argentina can be expected.
subfiles.summary: Requests an expected date for archival information on Japanese subversive activities in Argentina.

subfiles.title: Review of letters written aboard SS Wild Hunter
subfiles.about: Reports the FBI’s review of letters written aboard the SS Wild Hunter.
subfiles.summary: The FBI found only harmless personal material in the bundle of letters.

subfiles.title: Referral of SS Wild Hunter letters for examination
subfiles.about: Asks whether shipboard letters contain information on Japanese activities in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Sends the letters for examination before forwarding them through the Embassy to their addressees.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Ofelia P. Fernández
subfiles.about: Forwards an FBI report based on interrogation of Japanese repatriates.
subfiles.summary: Sends new information on Fernández gathered from repatriates interviewed in California.

subfiles.title: FBI interrogation report on Ofelia P. Fernández
subfiles.about: Records Masao Tsuda’s account of Fernández’s standing and contacts in the Japanese community.
subfiles.summary: Tsuda called Fernández well known among Japanese residents and close to a naval attaché and correspondent; he could not confirm intelligence work.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Angel A. Perrone
subfiles.about: Forwards an FBI interrogation report on alleged Japanese informant Angel A. Perrone.
subfiles.summary: Sends information obtained from Japanese repatriates interviewed in California.

subfiles.title: FBI interrogation report on Angel A. Perrone
subfiles.about: Records Tsuda’s account of payments to Perrone for information sought by Japanese attachés.
subfiles.summary: Tsuda said he passed payments from naval and military attachés to Perrone, who supplied Argentine political and military information. Tsuda doubted its quality.

subfiles.title: Embassy request for investigation of Japanese organizations and espionage
subfiles.about: Requests prioritized information on Japanese espionage, schools, associations, secret societies and gardeners’ organizations in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy asks for intelligence from Japan on espionage agents, communications, funding, school control, associations and suspected secret societies. It requests priorities in the order listed and identification of information unsuitable for sharing with Argentina’s Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for Buenos Aires despatch 584
subfiles.about: Routes despatch 584 from Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Routes the Embassy despatch on Kingo Kawai.

subfiles.title: Despatch enclosing note verbale on Kingo Kawai
subfiles.about: Encloses a note verbale giving Argentine authorities supplementary information on Kingo Kawai.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Embassy’s August 8 reply to Argentina’s request for information on Kawai.

subfiles.title: Note verbale on Kingo Kawai’s alleged espionage network
subfiles.to: Argentine Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship
subfiles.about: Supplies allegations about Kawai’s leadership of Japanese maritime espionage in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy identifies four reported members of Kawai’s network and says they operated as trawler crewmen and later in Argentine port cities.

subfiles.title: State Department forwarding of Kawai despatch to Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of despatch 584 on Kingo Kawai to naval intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Sends two copies of the Embassy’s confidential Kawai despatch.

subfiles.title: State Department forwarding of Kawai despatch to Army
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of despatch 584 on Kingo Kawai to military intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Sends three copies of the Embassy’s confidential Kawai despatch.

subfiles.title: Argentine request for information on German and Japanese organizations
subfiles.about: Reports an Argentine Foreign Ministry request for information about listed German and Japanese organizations.
subfiles.summary: Lists organizations and Buenos Aires addresses for which the Argentine Foreign Ministry seeks information.
